acceptanceCriteria: A spec (new or an amendment to tasks-criterion-binding-v0.md) defines the gate input: the sealed cem/1.0 result's `verdict` object and `verdictSha256` (CEM-V1-086), the minimum tier per touched path, and the refusal codes for a missing, unsealed or disagreeing verdict; numbered requirements, non-goals and rollback are recorded.

`corvint-tasks gate run` with the new gate evaluates a committed cem/1.0 map and records PASS/FAIL with the verdictSha256 and the per-path minimum tier in the gate result; a control with a producer-edited tier value is refused because the consumer recomputes it.
Both the native verifier and interop/cem01-go produce the verdict the gate pins; a disagreement is a gate FAIL named `verifier-disagreement`, never a pass.
One real ticket in this queue is completed through the gate on a migrated map and its receipt audit is retained in the build log.
body: Source: review of CEM 1.0 fit for the Corvint and corvint-tasks use cases, 2026-10-12, orchestrating session for decision 0523/0525. Observed: corvint-tasks does not consume CEM maps today; internal/taskman imports internal/cem/wire only for the generic JSON value type, and docs/specs/tasks-criterion-binding-v0.md refuses to delegate completion authority to opaque cem/1.0-experimental.1 references. Decision 0523 P1 (CEM-V1-083) makes the criterion provider-neutral (any committed blob span) and a cem/1.0 map MUST verify with no Tasks store present, so the only existing link (CEM-V1-002 native ticket binding) becomes an optional extension. Consequence: after rc.3 a ticket's native completion and the change's sealed cem/1.0 verdict are two unconnected proofs of the same change. Expected: a Tasks gate can require the sealed verdict (verdictSha256 plus the consumer-computed citation block, CEM-V1-080..082/086) as evidence, for example `every hunk under the ticket's effects.touchPaths is at least anchored` or `held hunks >= N once V1-1266 lands`, with the verdict bytes pinned in the gate result and re-verifiable by either independent consumer. Non-goals: Tasks never raises a tier, never trusts a producer-written field, and completion authority stays with the native store (TCB-V0-006). Open question for the spec: whether the gate reads the committed map from the primary checkout at the attempt's snapshot head or receives the verdict as an attached-evidence receipt.
title: corvint-tasks gate consumes the sealed cem/1.0 verdict as gate evidence
